highlights: A SCAP directive overhauled public assistance into a centralized relief system based strictly on need, abolishing preferential pensions and aid for military ex-servicemen.
An emergency mass DDT dusting campaign in Osaka reached over 90 percent of the population to suppress a typhus outbreak that exceeded 400 cases.
Relief reserves from returned military stocks began distribution, including 430,000 blankets, 150,000 overcoats, 200,000 uniforms and 111,457 metric tons of cereals.
Smallpox vaccine production rose sharply, surpassing the February goal of 10,250,000 doses, to combat smallpox outbreaks across Japan.
Repatriation through 24 February 1946 totaled 768,209 Koreans, 30,695 Chinese, 18,532 Formosans, 12,187 Ryukyuans and 1,465,980 returning Japanese.
Japanese authorities ordered nationwide confiscation of heroin and set deadlines for prosecuting unauthorized possession of the narcotic.
Of 5,932 dentists displaced by wartime bombing, 2,579 were rehabilitated and re-established in practice, though equipment shortages persisted.
A new Ministry of Health public health nursing curriculum takes effect in April 1946, with plans assisted for a Kyushu training institute.

summary: This February 1946 monthly report details public health, welfare administration, and disease control across occupied Japan during early post-surrender reconstruction. Key developments center on SCAP directives reforming Japanese relief administration into a centralized, non-discriminatory public assistance program that explicitly abolished military pensions and preferential treatment for ex-servicemen. To avert humanitarian crisis, Occupation authorities released former military stocks—including over 111,000 metric tons of cereals and 430,000 blankets—and supervised relief for foreign nationals. In public health, the report highlights an aggressive response to an escalating Osaka typhus outbreak through a mass DDT dusting campaign reaching over 90 percent of the city's populace, alongside rapid expansion of smallpox vaccine production exceeding 10 million doses monthly. The report also documents the rehabilitation of 2,579 bombing-displaced dentists, a new national public health nursing curriculum, and strict narcotics controls including nationwide heroin confiscation. Historians will find valuable quantitative baselines on social insurance funds, civilian hospital capacity, communicable disease curves, and repatriation flows tracking 829,000 repatriated foreign nationals and 1.46 million returning Japanese, illustrating the institutional transition from Imperial wartime systems to demilitarized civilian governance.
